zh.title: 一句话故事：谁想要什么，被什么挡住
zh.summary: 把模糊的想法压成一句能拍的话：一个具体的人，想要一个具体的东西，被一个具体的障碍挡住。

zh.title: 分镜表：把一句话拆成 8 个能拍的镜头
zh.summary: 画得丑没关系，现场看得懂就行。一张分镜表只回答三件事：谁、在哪、下一个动作是什么。

zh.title: 三幕片的骨架：把人物往墙上逼
zh.summary: 第一幕给目标，第二幕加阻力，第三幕让选择发生。每一幕只做一件事。

zh.title: 拍不演戏的人：别让他演，给他一件事做
zh.summary: 采访对象、店主、家人，越说“自然一点”越僵。给他一个具体动作，一句他自己的话，摄影机往后退一点。

zh.title: 采访别问“你有什么感受”：把问题换成动作
zh.summary: 一个人回忆不起“感受”，但记得那天先迈了哪只脚。问题越具体，回答越像人话。

zh.title: 对白：让人物用嘴争，不用嘴解释
zh.summary: 对白写不动，常常是因为把人物想说的话都写了出来。好对白每句都在争一个东西，听的人有反应，背景交给画面。

zh.title: 冲突：两个人都得有道理
zh.summary: 吵架不等于冲突。真正的冲突，是两个人要的东西都合理，但只能有一个结果。观众得同时看懂两边，才会替他们难受。

zh.title: 人物弧光：不是变好，是选择变了
zh.summary: 弧光不是人物从坏变好。是同一个压力下，他第一次选了安全，最后一次选了代价。观众看到的是选择变了，不是性格标签换了。

zh.title: 旁白：别替观众总结
zh.summary: 旁白不是把画面再说一遍。它要么给画面没有的信息，要么给一个人的判断。能拍出来就别念；要念，就短、具体、带偏见。

zh.title: 欲望与赌注：输了会失去什么
zh.summary: 人物想要什么不重要，重要的是得不到会失去什么。

zh.title: 场景描述：只写镜头拍得到的
zh.summary: 场景描述只写镜头拍得到的东西：光、动作、物件、声音；心理活动留给演员。

zh.title: 镜头表：镜号、景别、动作、时长
zh.summary: 镜头表四列就够：镜号、景别、动作、时长；写不清这四样，现场一定乱。

zh.title: 排练：先走位，再给台词
zh.summary: 排练先走位，台词可以拿在手上；身体站对了，话才有地方落。

zh.title: 障碍升级：同一堵墙越收越紧
zh.summary: 同一个障碍连撞三次，每次代价更高，观众才会觉得人物真的被逼到墙角。

zh.title: 中点转向：换方法，不换目标
zh.summary: 中点不是反转剧情，而是人物换一种办法去要同一个东西。

zh.title: 场景序列：三场戏推一个变化
zh.summary: 一场戏只完成一个变化，三场戏连起来才推得动一个段落。

zh.title: 支线：只留能压主线的一条
zh.summary: 支线不是增加热闹，它要在某个时刻把主线逼得更紧。

zh.title: 主题：让人物做出来，不让他说出来
zh.summary: 主题不要让人物讲出来，让他在压力下做一个能暴露价值观的选择。

zh.title: 结尾：停在选择之后
zh.summary: 结尾停在选择之后，别再加一段解释；观众自己补上的那句更有力。

zh.title: 短片经济：删掉拍不起的东西
zh.summary: 短片先删掉拍不起的场面，再把剩下的东西写得更具体。

zh.title: 剧本格式：让全组读得懂
zh.summary: 剧本格式不是给文学奖看的，它要让摄影、录音和剪辑一眼找到信息。

zh.title: 改稿：先删解释，再补动作
zh.summary: 改稿先删解释，再补一个能看见的动作；两件事常常是同一件事。

zh.title: 潜台词：台词下面那件事
zh.summary: 潜台词是人物嘴上说 A、心里要 B；导演的工作是让观众看见那个 B。

zh.title: 独白：别让人物对着空气演讲
zh.summary: 独白不是人物对空气演讲，他得有一个不想听、却又走不开的听众。

zh.title: 短剧剧本：30 秒一个钩子
zh.summary: 短剧剧本按“钩子—反转—留扣”写，每三十秒必须发生一件改变局面的事。

zh.title: 改编：从真实事件到可拍剧本
zh.summary: 改编不是复述事件，而是找到一个能在两个小时里被拍出来的冲突。

zh.title: 读稿会：只记三个问题
zh.summary: 读稿会只记三类问题：听不懂、不想看、人物不像。别开成剧本研讨会。

zh.title: 场与场之间：用动作接，不用字幕
zh.summary: 场与场之间用动作、声音或物件接，别用字幕卡解释“三天后”。

zh.title: 喜剧：先搭预期，再拆
zh.summary: 喜剧先让观众准确预测下一秒，再只拆掉一个关键条件。

zh.title: 插入镜头：一个细节顶一句台词
zh.summary: 一个插入镜头能顶掉一句台词：手抖、杯沿、没关的门，都比解释有用。

zh.title: 段落分镜：一场戏怎么排镜头
zh.summary: 段落分镜不是把剧本一句一句画出来，而是决定这场戏先给观众看什么。

zh.title: 动态分镜：先定时长，再补画
zh.summary: 动态分镜先定镜头时长和剪辑点，画得糙没关系，节奏错了才是大问题。

zh.title: 分镜评审：让摄影和剪辑先挑错
zh.summary: 分镜评审让摄影先挑机位、剪辑先挑缺口，导演最后决定改哪三格。

zh.title: 给演员调整：只给动词，不给形容词
zh.summary: 给演员调整时给动词：走慢点、压住火、别碰她；别给“再自然一点”。

zh.title: 群戏：让每个人都有事做
zh.summary: 群戏里每个人都有事做，观众才相信这是一个真实的空间，而不是一排等台词的人。

zh.title: 表演尺度：镜头越近，动作越小
zh.summary: 镜头越近，动作越小；远景里刚好的手势，近景里会像演戏。

zh.title: 复试：用同一段动作对比
zh.summary: 复试别让演员重新演一段，让两个人做同一个动作，才看得出差别。

zh.title: 拍孩子：给任务，不给指令
zh.summary: 拍孩子给任务不给指令：把桌上的杯子递给我，比“演得难过一点”有用。

zh.title: 第一次当导演：先保表演，再保机位
zh.summary: 第一次当导演，先保住演员和一场戏，再想着多拍几个机位。

zh.title: 给演员的笔记：一句能执行的话
zh.summary: 给演员的笔记一句就够，而且要能执行；三句建议等于没有建议。

zh.title: 场景发动机：欲望、障碍、转折
zh.summary: 场景不是信息交换，而是一个人想要东西、被挡住、被迫改变。

zh.title: 对白潜台词：一个人也能演
zh.summary: 好对白不是把心里话说出来，而是让角色说一件事、做另一件事。

zh.title: 结构转折：中点、结尾、格式
zh.summary: 结构不是三幕模板，而是中点把方向翻一次、结尾把选择付一次代价。

zh.title: 表演指导：排练、给笔记、尺度
zh.summary: 表演指导不是喊“再来一条”，而是把动作、意图和尺度变成演员能执行的话。

zh.title: 覆盖与分镜：从 Shot Sheet 到 Animatic
zh.summary: 分镜不是画得漂亮，而是 shot sheet、coverage 和 animatic 能在剪辑台上兑现。

zh.title: 场景缝合：转场、插入、看板
zh.summary: 场景之间不是靠转场特效接上，而是靠一个未完成的动作和下一场的第一个信息。

zh.title: 物件叙事：让道具替一句台词
zh.summary: 道具不是背景；当人物主动使用它、它发生变化、最后留在画面里，它就能替一句解释台词。

zh.title: 无对白场景：不靠台词讲完一段
zh.summary: 删掉台词不等于无对白；无对白要靠欲望、动作、障碍和代价四件事，把信息变成可见的变化。

en.title: The One-Line Story: Who Wants What, and What Stands in the Way
en.summary: Compress a vague idea into a shootable sentence: a specific person, a specific want, and a specific obstacle.

en.title: The Shot Sheet: Turn One Line into Eight Shootable Shots
en.summary: It can look rough. The crew just needs to read it. One shot sheet answers three things: who, where, and what happens next.

en.title: Three Acts: Put the Character Against a Wall
en.summary: Act one gives a goal, act two applies pressure, act three forces a choice. Each act does one job.

en.title: Directing Non-Actors: Give Them a Task, Not a Performance
en.summary: The more you tell a real person to act natural, the stiffer they get. Give them a task, their own words, and a little more distance.

en.title: Stop Asking “How Did You Feel”: Ask for an Action
en.summary: People rarely remember a feeling. They remember which foot they moved first. Specific questions get human answers.

en.title: Dialogue: Let Them Fight with Words, Not Explain
en.summary: Dialogue stalls when the writer says everything the character is thinking. Good lines fight for something, the listener reacts, and the backstory stays on screen.

en.title: Conflict: Both Sides Need a Point
en.summary: An argument is not conflict. Real conflict is two valid wants that cannot both win. The audience has to understand both sides before it can hurt.

en.title: Character Arc: Not Better, Different Choices
en.summary: An arc is not a character turning good. Under the same pressure, they first choose safety and finally choose the cost. The audience sees the choice change, not a new personality label.

en.title: Voice-Over: Do Not Summarize What the Picture Already Says
en.summary: Voice-over is not the picture read aloud. It either gives information the picture cannot, or gives one person's judgment. If you can shoot it, do not say it. If you must say it, keep it short, concrete, and biased.

en.title: Want and Stakes: What Does Losing Cost?
en.summary: What a character wants matters less than what losing it costs.

en.title: Scene Description: Only What the Camera Can See
en.summary: Describe only what the camera can see: light, action, objects, sound. Leave inner life to the actor.

en.title: Shot Sheet: Number, Framing, Action, Duration
en.summary: Four columns are enough: number, framing, action, duration. If these are vague, the set will be chaos.

en.title: Rehearsal: Block First, Lines Later
en.summary: Block first, scripts in hand. Once the body is in the right place, the lines have somewhere to land.

en.title: Escalation: Same Wall, Higher Cost
en.summary: Hit the same obstacle three times and raise the cost each time; only then does the character look cornered.

en.title: Midpoint Turn: Change the Method, Not the Goal
en.summary: The midpoint is not a plot twist; it is the character changing methods to pursue the same want.

en.title: A Sequence: Three Scenes, One Change
en.summary: One scene delivers one change; three scenes together move a sequence.

en.title: Subplot: Only the One That Presses the Main Line
en.summary: A subplot is not extra noise; it must squeeze the main line at one specific point.

en.title: Theme Through Action, Not Speeches
en.summary: Do not let a character speak the theme; make them choose under pressure and reveal it.

en.title: Ending: Stop After the Choice
en.summary: End after the choice. The sentence the audience supplies is stronger than a closing explanation.

en.title: Short-Film Economy: Cut What You Cannot Shoot
en.summary: Cut what you cannot shoot, then make what remains more specific.

en.title: Script Format: Make the Whole Crew Read It the Same Way
en.summary: Script format is not for a literary prize; it helps camera, sound, and edit find information at a glance.

en.title: Rewrite: Delete the Explanation, Add the Action
en.summary: In a rewrite, delete the explanation and add a visible action; often they are the same fix.

en.title: Subtext: The Thing Under the Line
en.summary: Subtext is saying A while needing B; the director's job is to let the audience see the B.

en.title: Monologue: Give It a Listener and a Block
en.summary: A monologue needs a listener who cannot easily leave and does not quite want to hear it.

en.title: Short Drama: A Hook Every Thirty Seconds
en.summary: Short drama runs on hook, turn, cliff: every thirty seconds something must change the board.

en.title: Adaptation: From Real Event to Shootable Scene
en.summary: Adaptation is not retelling an event; it is finding a conflict that can be shot within two hours.

en.title: Table Read: Listen for Three Problems Only
en.summary: A table read tracks three problems only: unclear, boring, out of character. Do not turn it into a seminar.

en.title: Scene Transitions: Carry an Action Across the Cut
en.summary: Carry an action, a sound, or an object across the cut instead of using a title card to explain time.

en.title: Comedy: Build the Expectation, Then Break It
en.summary: Comedy lets the audience predict the next beat, then removes one crucial condition.

en.title: Insert Shot: One Detail Beats One Line
en.summary: An insert can replace a line: a shaking hand, a cup rim, an open door.

en.title: Sequence Board: Shoot the Scene, Not the Script
en.summary: A sequence board does not illustrate every line; it decides what the audience sees first.

en.title: Animatic: Time the Scene Before You Draw It
en.summary: An animatic fixes shot length and cut points first; rough drawings are fine, wrong rhythm is not.

en.title: Board Review: Let Camera and Edit Find the Gaps
en.summary: In a board review, camera finds positions, edit finds gaps, and the director chooses three panels to fix.

en.title: Adjusting Actors: Give Verbs, Not Adjectives
en.summary: Give actors verbs: slower, hold the anger, do not touch her. Never "be more natural."

en.title: Ensemble Scene: Give Everyone a Task
en.summary: In an ensemble scene everyone has a task; only then does the space feel real instead of a row of waiting actors.

en.title: Performance Scale: Closer Camera, Smaller Action
en.summary: The closer the camera, the smaller the action; a gesture that works wide looks acted in a close-up.

en.title: Callback: Compare the Same Action
en.summary: In a callback, do not give a new scene; give the same action and compare.

en.title: Directing Children: Give a Task, Not a Line Reading
en.summary: With children, give a task, not an instruction: hand me the cup beats "look sad."

en.title: Directing Debut: Protect Performance Before Coverage
en.summary: On a first directing job, protect the performance and the scene before chasing more coverage.

en.title: Notes to Actors: One Executable Sentence
en.summary: One executable sentence is enough for an actor; three suggestions add up to none.

en.title: Scene engine: want, obstacle, turn
en.summary: A scene is not information exchange; someone wants something, is blocked, and has to change.

en.title: Dialogue subtext: one person can play
en.summary: Good dialogue does not say the inner truth; a character says one thing and does another.

en.title: Structure turn: midpoint, ending, format
en.summary: Structure is not a three-act template; the midpoint turns direction and the ending charges for the choice.

en.title: Performance direction: rehearsal, notes, scale
en.summary: Direction is not shouting one more; it turns action, intention and scale into playable notes.

en.title: Coverage board: shot sheet to animatic
en.summary: A board is not a pretty drawing; shot sheet, coverage and animatic must cash out on the timeline.

en.title: Scene stitch: transition, insert, board
en.summary: Scenes connect through an unfinished action and the next scene's first information, not a transition effect.

en.title: Object Storytelling: Let a Prop Carry the Line
en.summary: A prop is not background. When a character uses it, it changes, and it remains in the frame, it can carry a line that would otherwise be explained.

en.title: The Silent Scene: Tell It Without Dialogue
en.summary: Removing lines is not a silent scene. Silence needs want, action, obstacle and cost so information becomes a visible change.
